answer: Sybil wallets that wander into a network gain no stake unless they first echo a costly proof of work back to the chain, so each fake identity must burn real computation. When the proof's difficulty scales with the value an identity can claim, the cost of minting a thousand ghosts exceeds the profit of gaming one honest node. The bottleneck: attackers must buy real work for every mask, while honest agents pay once and keep the ivory tower of their reputation intact.
